solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Broadcasts in blimp (7)

blocks.note: a station airs a programme when it broadcasts it

annotation.surface: A radio station putting out its shows from a hovering blimp.
annotation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a joining word placing the broadcasts inside the blimp, but it is a piece of wordplay: in, meaning trendy, is HIP.
annotation.definitionFit: A blimp is a non-rigid airship, kept aloft by gas.

entries.clue: Polar boat twinkling, it’s said (6)

indicatorNotes.it’s said: what is said is heard rather than read, so the pieces are sounds, not spellings

blocks.note: in a twinkling = in a tick, a moment

annotation.surface: A little boat glinting on a polar sea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'twinkling' reads as sparkle, but it is the noun for an instant, as in 'the twinkling of an eye'; a tick is British for a moment.
annotation.definitionFit: Arctic means belonging to the North Polar region.

entries.clue: Designate to someone else authentic patch of land (7)

blocks.note: a lot is a plot of ground

annotation.surface: Handing over a genuine plot of land to a new owner.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition runs to four words, and the surface reads straight through it into the wordplay, which is what hides the join.
annotation.definitionFit: To reallot something is to allot it again, assigning it to a different person.

entries.clue: Parks, maybe, kept most of river patrols for old lizard (9)

indicatorNotes.most of: most of a word is all but its last letter
indicatorNotes.patrols: a guard patrols around a place, so HAD and UR go around ROSA

blocks.note: kept = had, as in had a dog
the River Ure in Yorkshire, minus its last letter
Rosa Parks, the US civil rights campaigner; 'maybe' flags her as one example of a Parks

annotation.surface: Park rangers who kept watch on a river looking out for some ancient reptile.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital P on Parks is the giveaway that a person is meant; in the surface it passes for the start of a sentence about parkland.
annotation.definitionFit: A hadrosaur is a duck-billed dinosaur, and dinosaurs are loosely called old lizards.

entries.clue: Model cuddles small group (5)

indicatorNotes.cuddles: to cuddle is to hold in your arms, so POSE holds S

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A fashion model hugging a few friends.
annotation.walkthrough: 'small group' reads as one phrase, but 'small' belongs to the wordplay and 'group' stands alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A posse is a band of people, originally one summoned by a sheriff.

entries.clue: AI not ready, for the most part, to overturn nation (7)

indicatorNotes.for the most part: most of a word is all but its last letter
indicatorNotes.to overturn: overturning turns the string over, so it reads right to left

blocks.note: ready = set, losing its last letter

annotation.surface: A worry that artificial intelligence, still half-built, could bring down a government.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a headline about artificial intelligence toppling a government, but AI is just two letters, and 'overturn' means reading the whole string backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic nation, independent since 1991.

entries.clue: Uneven growth of evergreen pruned in East Yorkshire’s capital (8)

indicatorNotes.pruned: pruning cuts the end off, so PINASTER loses ER
indicatorNotes.in: the cut tree goes inside E and Y

blocks.note: the capital, first, letter of Yorkshire
the pinaster, or maritime pine, trimmed of ER

annotation.surface: A gardener noticing a lopsided pine in the heart of East Yorkshire.
annotation.walkthrough: 'capital' tempts the solver to look for a town such as Hull; in crosswords a word's capital is its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Epinasty is botanical: a leaf or stem curves because its upper side grows faster than the lower.

entries.clue: Agreement to shorten free entertainment (5)

indicatorNotes.to shorten: shortening a word takes off its end, so TREATY loses Y

blocks.note: a treaty, minus its last letter

annotation.surface: Negotiators agreeing to cut short a free show.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is two words at the end; 'free' is part of it, not an anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A treat is something enjoyable that someone else pays for, such as a free outing.

entries.clue: Idiot bishop interrupts mining and teaching groups (7)

indicatorNotes.interrupts: to interrupt is to break into, so B goes between NUM and NUT

blocks.note: the National Union of Teachers; 'groups' covers both unions
B = bishop, as in chess notation

annotation.surface: A foolish cleric barging into a meeting of two trade unions.
annotation.walkthrough: The NUM and NUT are two British trade unions, for miners and for teachers.
annotation.definitionFit: Numbnut is slang for a stupid person.

entries.clue: Cursing obsessive, conceptual carols, each lacking a conclusion (14)

indicatorNotes.each lacking a conclusion: every piece loses its last letter

blocks.note: anal, as in anal-retentive, minus L

annotation.surface: Someone muttering oaths at a fussy, over-intellectual set of Christmas carols.
annotation.walkthrough: The three words look like a critic's list of adjectives, but each must be turned into a synonym and then clipped before joining.
annotation.definitionFit: To anathematise is to curse or formally denounce.

entries.clue: Eucalyptus currently faces round houses (4,3)

indicatorNotes.round: going round turns MUGS back to front
indicatorNotes.houses: the turned word houses NOW, holding it inside

annotation.surface: A gum tree that now looks out on a ring of houses.
annotation.walkthrough: 'round' reads with 'faces' as a direction to look, but it turns MUGS round instead.
annotation.definitionFit: The snow gum is an Australian eucalyptus of the high country.

entries.clue: Wastes question probing colonel? (9)

indicatorNotes.probing: a probe goes inside, so QU enters SANDERS

blocks.note: Colonel Sanders, founder of KFC; the question mark flags that he is one example
QU is a standard abbreviation for question

annotation.surface: An officer under interrogation over money gone to waste.
annotation.walkthrough: 'colonel' looks like a rank; it names a particular colonel, the fried-chicken one.
annotation.definitionFit: To squander is to waste, especially money or chances.

entries.clue: Wrestling champion from Australia with necktie ejecting odd characters (5)

indicatorNotes.ejecting odd characters: throwing out the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters leaves the even ones

annotation.surface: An Australian wrestling star made to take off his odd tie.
annotation.walkthrough: The champion is a sumo one, so there is no Australian in the answer; OZ only lends its letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Ozeki is the second-highest rank in professional sumo, just below yokozuna.

entries.clue: Criminal hurrying on caged animals competing against each other (9,6)

indicatorNotes.Criminal: a criminal version is a corrupted one, so the letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: A crook hurrying past some caged beasts as they are set against one another.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder is apt: the dogs are held in traps, a kind of cage, then hurry round the track.
annotation.definitionFit: Greyhound racing is the sport of dogs racing each other round a track.

entries.clue: Artist’s friend concealing biases from time to time (7)

indicatorNotes.concealing: MATE conceals the letters, holding them inside
indicatorNotes.from time to time: now and then means every other letter

annotation.surface: A painter's pal who now and then hides his prejudices.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Artist's friend' reads as one possessive phrase; the 's is 'is', joining the artist to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a French painter, leader of the Fauves.

entries.clue: Concealed chlorine can ultimately damage clothing range (11)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: the ultimate letter of damage is E
indicatorNotes.clothing: CL, TIN and E wrap round ANDES like clothes

blocks.note: Cl is the symbol for chlorine
the Andes, the South American mountain range

annotation.surface: A hidden canister of chlorine that could harm a line of clothes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'clothing range' reads as a fashion line, but 'clothing' is the instruction to wrap and the range is the mountains.
annotation.definitionFit: Clandestine means kept secret or concealed.

entries.clue: Evaluation intended to protect stable setter (11)

indicatorNotes.to protect: MEANT goes round SURE ME like a shield

blocks.note: stable = sure, as in sure footing
the setter refers to themself as me

annotation.surface: An assessment meant to keep a horse's stable safe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'stable setter' suggests something that sets a horse's stable, but these are two words: steady, and the crossword's own setter.
annotation.definitionFit: A measurement is an assessment of size or amount.

entries.clue: Large potato dish, but no starters, in northern home (5)

indicatorNotes.no starters: each word loses its first letter

blocks.note: aloo, an Indian potato dish, minus A

annotation.surface: A restaurant serving a big potato dish with no starters, in a house far up north.
annotation.walkthrough: 'starters' sounds like a menu's first course, which fits the dish; here it means first letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An igloo is the Inuit snow house of the Arctic.

entries.clue: Protein from eastern tip of Fife, latest to arrive (7)

indicatorNotes.eastern tip of: in an across entry east is the right-hand end, so the last letter of Fife

blocks.note: a train that is in has arrived

annotation.surface: A protein shipped in from the eastern end of Fife, the most recent delivery.
annotation.walkthrough: Fife is a Scottish county whose east end really is a point, East Neuk, but the tip wanted is the last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Elastin is the stretchy protein in skin and blood vessels.

entries.clue: Celebrations in mountains welcoming new leader of Nepal (3,6)

indicatorNotes.leader of: the leader of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A festival in the Himalayas greeting Nepal's new head of state.
annotation.walkthrough: A hen night is the British name for a bride's party with her friends before the wedding.
annotation.definitionFit: Hen nights are pre-wedding celebrations for the bride-to-be.

entries.clue: I tape neurotransmitter to rock at which material change occurs (10,11)

annotation.surface: Someone recording a brain chemical so that it can be set to music.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a description, not a synonym: it names the temperature by what happens there, so it reads as 'the point at which...'.
annotation.definitionFit: A transition temperature is the point at which a substance changes phase or structure, such as melting or becoming superconducting.

entries.clue: Really bored by About A Boy, climb over wall (7)

indicatorNotes.bored by: SO is bored through, so the other letters sit inside it

blocks.note: so = really, as in so good

annotation.surface: A viewer so bored by the film About a Boy that they want to escape over the wall.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitals make About A Boy look like the Nick Hornby title; split up, it is C, A and LAD.
annotation.definitionFit: A scalado, or escalade, is the scaling of a wall with ladders in an assault.

entries.clue: Delighted Scottish sweetheart blocking “extremely” entering dictionary (9)

indicatorNotes.blocking: JO blocks the path through VERY by standing in it

blocks.note: jo is a Scots word for a sweetheart, as in Burns's John Anderson, my jo

annotation.surface: A Scots lover thrilled to see a word added to the dictionary.
annotation.walkthrough: Two containers nest, one inside the other; the inverted commas round 'extremely' signal that the word itself is being treated as an item.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, turned up a notch: joy running over its brim is delight at its fullest.

entries.clue: I own property next door — area with goat? (7)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition speaks as the answer: an abutter would say this of themself

blocks.note: a goat is known for ramming with its head, so it is one who does that; the question mark admits the stretch

annotation.surface: A neighbour boasting of land next door that comes with a goat.
annotation.walkthrough: BUTTER here rhymes with putter: one who butts, which a goat is known for.
annotation.definitionFit: An abutter is the owner of property that touches another's.

entries.clue: Female giving in, ignoring yen for magistrate and satirist (8)

indicatorNotes.ignoring: ignoring the Y means leaving it out

blocks.note: Y = yen, the Japanese currency; this is the letter removed

annotation.surface: A woman yielding to pressure, no longer longing for a judge who writes satire.
annotation.walkthrough: 'yen' reads as longing, but it is the currency's symbol. Henry Fielding wrote Tom Jones and was a London magistrate.
annotation.definitionFit: Henry Fielding was both a Bow Street magistrate and a satirical novelist.

entries.clue: Relaxed and performing well, walk out of bounds (8)

indicatorNotes.out of bounds: the bounds are the edges; take them out and the middle is left

annotation.surface: A cricketer at ease and on form, strolling beyond the boundary.
annotation.walkthrough: 'out of bounds' sounds like a place you may not walk; here it strips the bounds, the outer letters, from walk.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal means relaxed, not following strict rules of form.

entries.clue: Collected skirts in that woman’s home; time I did embroidery (15)

indicatorNotes.skirts: to skirt something is to go round its edge, so FETCHED goes round the rest

blocks.note: to fetch someone is to collect them
at hers, that is, at her house

annotation.surface: Someone who, once picked up, spent an evening at a friend's house doing needlework.
annotation.walkthrough: 'skirts' looks like clothing to go with the embroidery, but it is a verb meaning goes around; 'that woman's home' is the idiom 'at hers'.
annotation.definitionFit: Featherstitch is a zigzag embroidery stitch, so to featherstitch is to do that embroidery.

entries.clue: Consider proper payments to be returned before sex (3,3)

indicatorNotes.to be returned: returned means sent back, so FEES reads right to left

blocks.note: fees are payments for a service
it is a coy word for sex

annotation.surface: Payments that must be refunded before anything intimate happens.
annotation.walkthrough: 'proper' reads with 'payments' as a description of fair fees, but it belongs to the definition, 'Consider proper'.
annotation.definitionFit: The idiom, as in 'do as you see fit', means to judge something right, so the two-word definition matches it verb for verb.

entries.clue: Enjoyable collection of books about lady’s buttocks (9)

indicatorNotes.about: about can mean beside or near, so NT is placed alongside DAME

blocks.note: a dame is a titled lady
the New Testament, a collection of the books of the Bible

annotation.surface: A cheeky, entertaining anthology about a woman's bottom.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining the wordplay to a jokey old word for the backside.
annotation.definitionFit: Fundament is a humorous, old-fashioned word for the buttocks.

entries.clue: Squeeze Quebec into Rough Guides (7)

indicatorNotes.into: 'squeeze into' is the sense: the letter is pushed inside the jumbled word

blocks.note: Quebec is Q in the NATO alphabet
GUIDES rearranged, with Q entering after S

annotation.surface: Cramming a section on Quebec into a Rough Guide travel book.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital R makes Rough Guides the travel-book series; 'Rough' is the anagram indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: To squidge is British informal for to squash or squeeze.

entries.clue: Footballing legend backing Chinese team, initially, for big game (8)

indicatorNotes.backing: in a down entry backing sends PELE upwards, reversed

blocks.note: the Han are China's majority people

annotation.surface: A football great supporting a Chinese side in an important match.
annotation.walkthrough: 'big game' reads as a crucial match, which fits the football; it is also the hunter's term for large wild animals.
annotation.definitionFit: Big game means large animals hunted for sport, and the elephant is the biggest.

entries.clue: Casually browsing very big boxes in sailing vessels (6-8)

indicatorNotes.boxes: to box something is to enclose it, so WHOPPING goes round IN DOWS

blocks.note: dow is a variant spelling of dhow, an Arab sailing boat

annotation.surface: Huge crates stowed aboard sailing ships.
annotation.walkthrough: 'boxes' reads as a noun for cargo stowed on ships; it is a verb, and the enclosed pieces go in after the first letter of the outer word.
annotation.definitionFit: Window-shopping is looking at goods in shop windows with no plan to buy.

entries.clue: Many young men broken by love (5)

indicatorNotes.broken by: LADS is broken open and O goes in the gap

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

annotation.surface: Lots of young men left heartbroken by love.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the first word alone; 'Many young men' reads as a phrase but splits after 'Many'.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal usage, as in 'loads of people', where a load is a heap and so a large number.

entries.clue: Bruiser ran over carrying ham (7)

indicatorNotes.carrying: the words carry the answer inside them

annotation.surface: A heavy who knocked someone down while carrying a joint of meat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'ran over' reads as a hit-and-run, but it is only a string of letters holding the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Serrano is a Spanish dry-cured ham.

entries.clue: At first, Ant and Dec’s follower accepting offer for capital (7)

indicatorNotes.At first: what comes at first in a word is its opening letter, so only that is taken from Ant
indicatorNotes.accepting: A and JAN accept BID between them

blocks.note: a bid is an offer at auction

annotation.surface: A TV double act and a sidekick taking a bid for a city.
annotation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a British TV presenting duo, so Dec's follower looks like a fan; it is the month after December.
annotation.definitionFit: Abidjan was the capital of Ivory Coast until 1983 and is still its economic capital.

entries.clue: Base rejected part of street arts business (9)

indicatorNotes.rejected: rejected means thrown back, so the letters read right to left
indicatorNotes.part of: the answer is a part of the words that follow

annotation.surface: A company of street performers turned down for a grant.
annotation.walkthrough: The hidden letters run across three words and backwards, so the answer is invisible until read from the right.
annotation.definitionFit: In science and biology the word names the layer underneath, the surface something grows on or is built upon.

entries.clue: Thief knocked back food, mostly animal fat (7)

indicatorNotes.knocked back: knocking something back sends it backwards, so GRUB reverses
indicatorNotes.mostly: most of lard, losing its last letter

annotation.surface: A robber who wolfed down a fatty meal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' reads as ate or drank quickly, which suits food; it is the reversal instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A burglar is a thief who breaks into buildings.

entries.clue: Anglo-American novelist found in legendary forest on island (9)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across entry, the forest put on the island comes after it

annotation.surface: A writer discovered living in a mythical wood on an island.
annotation.walkthrough: Christopher Isherwood was English-born and became a US citizen, hence Anglo-American.
annotation.definitionFit: Christopher Isherwood wrote Goodbye to Berlin and took US citizenship in 1946.

entries.clue: Conclusion from lazy worker, perhaps someone wanting more (7)

indicatorNotes.Conclusion from: the conclusion of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: a worker is one example of an earner

annotation.surface: An idle employee's verdict that someone else is always after more.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a lazy worker who wants more pay; the answer is the wanting, not the laziness.
annotation.definitionFit: A yearner is someone who longs for something.

entries.clue: Businessmen essentially adopted by wealthy former republic (5)

indicatorNotes.essentially: the essence of a word is its middle
indicatorNotes.adopted by: an adopted child is taken into a family, so the letter is taken into the word for wealthy

annotation.surface: Business leaders taken over by a rich former state.
annotation.walkthrough: The Weimar Republic's official name was still the German Reich, which is why a republic is fair.
annotation.definitionFit: Germany's Weimar Republic of 1919 to 1933 was officially the Deutsches Reich.

entries.clue: Aims to store rubidium in part of Glasgow (7)

indicatorNotes.to store: to store something is to keep it inside, as a cupboard stores food, so the aims hold the element

blocks.note: Rb is the symbol for rubidium

annotation.surface: A plan to keep a chemical stockpiled somewhere in Glasgow.
annotation.walkthrough: The Gorbals is a district of Glasgow, south of the Clyde.
annotation.definitionFit: The Gorbals is an inner-city area of Glasgow.

entries.clue: Ready replacement set to retain standard at equal intervals (5,4)

indicatorNotes.to retain: to retain is to keep hold of, so SET keeps the standard held inside it
indicatorNotes.at equal intervals: PAR goes in twice, once in each gap between the letters of SET

blocks.note: par is the standard, as in up to par, used twice

annotation.surface: A spare part kept ready, the set holding a standard piece at regular spacing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'at equal intervals' usually means alternate letters; here it spaces PAR evenly through S_E_T.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the component kept on hand in case the original breaks, ready to swap in.

entries.clue: With a cold, reported someone giving evidence in Cheshire town (6)

indicatorNotes.With a cold, reported: said through a blocked nose, T and SS thicken to D and N-ish sounds

blocks.note: the person in the box at a trial; say the word through a blocked nose

annotation.surface: A witness with a heavy cold testifying in a court in Cheshire.
annotation.walkthrough: Say witness with a heavy cold and the T and SS thicken into Widnes, a town on the Mersey in Cheshire, England.
annotation.definitionFit: Widnes is a town in Cheshire, on the north bank of the Mersey.

entries.clue: Potentially dangerous substance in leg? Learn with treatment (8)

indicatorNotes.with treatment: treated letters are worked on and rearranged

annotation.surface: A worrying substance found in a leg, and the patient told to learn about the treatment.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark after 'leg' breaks the surface in two; the fodder runs across it.
annotation.definitionFit: An allergen is a substance that triggers an allergic reaction, sometimes a dangerous one.

entries.clue: Being bigoted for this reason, without any introductions (9)

indicatorNotes.without any introductions: each word loses its introduction, its first letter

annotation.surface: Being narrow-minded for no stated reason, without even being introduced.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Being bigoted' reads as one phrase; 'Being' stands alone as the noun definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Being and existence both mean the state of existing.

entries.clue: Liberal has idle talk with a principal from Turkmenistan in their home? (8)

indicatorNotes.Liberal: a liberal version is freely treated, so HAS is rearranged
indicatorNotes.principal from: the principal letter of a word is its first

annotation.surface: A Liberal politician chatting with a head teacher from Turkmenistan at their house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'their' points back to the people of Turkmenistan, so their home is the country's capital; the question mark marks the stretch.
annotation.definitionFit: Ashgabat is the capital of Turkmenistan, home to its government and many of its people.

entries.clue: Free intensive care at old hospital hall — thanks to this? (8,6,7)

annotation.definition: Free intensive care at old hospital hall — thanks to this?

indicatorNotes.Free: freed letters are loosed and rearranged

anagram.fodder: INTENSIVE CARE AT O H HALL

blocks.note: H = hospital, as on road signs

annotation.surface: Intensive care given free in an old hospital building, and the institution to thank for it.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the NHS, Britain's state health system, is why hospital care there is free.
annotation.definitionFit: The National Health Service is Britain's publicly funded health system, free at the point of use.

entries.clue: Country, one with Africans, primarily (7)

blocks.note: the landlocked West African state named after its great river

annotation.surface: A country pictured as a place of Africans, above all.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Country' does double duty: it defines the answer and supplies NIGER, the neighbouring country whose name Nigeria extends.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition is the plain category: Africa's most populous state, a federal republic on the Gulf of Guinea.

entries.clue: Notice vice-president is offensive (7)

blocks.note: an ad is a notice in a paper

annotation.surface: A news notice declaring the vice-president offensive.
annotation.walkthrough: 'offensive' reads as rude, the natural sense after a politician; it is the noun for a military attack.
annotation.definitionFit: An advance is an offensive, a forward movement against the enemy.

entries.clue: Run away from uncle, perhaps, in case (7)

indicatorNotes.away from: R goes away from RELATIVE, leaving the rest

blocks.note: an uncle is one kind of relative; take away R
R = run, as on a cricket scoreboard; this is the letter removed

annotation.surface: A child fleeing an uncle, just in case.
annotation.walkthrough: 'case' reads as 'in case of trouble'; it is the grammatical sense. 'Run away' looks like fleeing but only removes R.
annotation.definitionFit: The elative is a grammatical case in Finnish and Hungarian meaning 'out of'.

entries.clue: Policemen hired to guard standing stone (6)

indicatorNotes.to guard: the words guard the answer, holding it inside

annotation.surface: Officers taken on to protect an ancient monument.
annotation.walkthrough: The scene fits: a menhir is exactly the sort of heritage site that might need guarding.
annotation.definitionFit: A menhir is a single tall prehistoric standing stone.

entries.clue: After reflecting, strip off, drunk, overindulging on vacation, and nod off (2,2,5)

indicatorNotes.After reflecting: a reflection is back to front, so the whole string reads right to left
indicatorNotes.on vacation: vacated, emptied of its middle, leaving the outer letters

blocks.note: to peel is to strip off

annotation.surface: A holidaymaker who, after some thought, undresses drunk from overdoing things and dozes off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'strip off' and 'drunk' read as a holiday scene; each is a piece, and the reversal applies to all three together.
annotation.definitionFit: Nodding off pictures the head dropping forward as a person drifts into sleep; the phrase is a plain idiomatic synonym.

entries.clue: Unhappy man’s letter to Israeli (5)

annotation.surface: A miserable man writing a letter to someone in Israel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'letter to Israeli' reads as correspondence; it means a letter of the Hebrew alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: Sadhe, or tsade, is the 18th letter of the Hebrew alphabet.

entries.clue: Faces six wise men (7)

blocks.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

annotation.surface: A group of six wise men confronting something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Faces' reads as a verb, confronts; it is the plural noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Visage is a literary word for a face or its expression, from the French; the plural matches 'Faces'.

entries.clue: Fight in part of tennis match if wife leaves (3-2)

indicatorNotes.leaves: W leaves the phrase, dropping out

blocks.note: set two, one part of a match, minus W
W = wife; this is the letter removed

annotation.surface: A row during a tennis set when the wife walks out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'part of tennis match' seems to be just SET; it is the whole of 'set two', from which W then goes.
annotation.definitionFit: The noun comes from setting to, getting stuck in, so it names a short sharp scrap or row.

entries.clue: Auditor’s to refer to appearance (5)

indicatorNotes.Auditor’s: an auditor is literally a hearer, so this is what a listener hears

blocks.note: to cite a source is to refer to it

annotation.surface: An accountant told to mention how things look.
annotation.walkthrough: An auditor looks like an accountant checking books; the word's root sense is a listener.
annotation.definitionFit: Sight can mean appearance, as in 'a sorry sight'.

entries.clue: Rant when I evicted commercial customers (5)

indicatorNotes.evicted: the I is thrown out of TIRADE

blocks.note: a tirade is a rant; take out I

annotation.surface: Someone ranting after being thrown out by the business's clients.
annotation.walkthrough: 'the trade' is the name for business buyers as opposed to the public, as in trade prices.
annotation.definitionFit: The trade means customers who buy for their businesses, as in 'trade only'.

entries.clue: Drinking the ordinary bubbly (11)

annotation.surface: Choosing the everyday fizz, not champagne.
annotation.walkthrough: 'bubbly' reads as a noun for champagne, and 'the ordinary' as its cheap cousin; it is an adjective telling you to churn.
annotation.definitionFit: Rehydration is taking in fluid, by drinking, to restore the body's water.

entries.clue: At first, bow tie night is awkward (2,5,4)

indicatorNotes.awkward: awkward letters sit wrongly, so they are rearranged

annotation.surface: A black-tie evening that feels uncomfortable at the start.
annotation.walkthrough: 'At first' looks like a first-letter instruction for 'bow'; here it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are sentence adverbs for the opening stage of something, as in 'to begin with, it rained'.

entries.clue: Decline stops parent’s sister listening (7)

indicatorNotes.stops: DIE stops up the middle of AUNT like a plug

blocks.note: an aunt is a parent's sister
to die away is to decline

annotation.surface: A deaf aunt whose hearing is starting to go.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Decline stops' reads as a falling-off that halts; 'stops' means plugs.
annotation.definitionFit: Audient is a rare adjective meaning listening or paying attention.

entries.clue: Try way to eat black cheese (7)

indicatorNotes.to eat: GO eats JET, taking it inside

blocks.note: have a go = have a try

annotation.surface: An invitation to sample a dark cheese.
annotation.walkthrough: 'black cheese' reads as one item, but the cheese is brown; black is the jet that GO swallows.
annotation.definitionFit: Gjetost is a sweet brown Norwegian goat's cheese.

entries.clue: Stars from ancient Egyptian city are both short (3,4)
